question: All of the following are true about Nizatidine except

options.opa: It is a H2 blocker used in peptic ulcer disease
options.opd: It can also lead to tachycardia

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Nizatidine" -> "H2 receptor antagonist" -> "used in peptic ulcer disease" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Nizatidine" -> "H2 receptor antagonist" -> "does not have 100% bioavailability" -> "typical bioavailability around 70%" -> 98%
CHAIN: "Nizatidine" -> "H2 receptor antagonist" -> "no significant effect on gastric emptying" -> "does not enhance gastric emptying" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Nizatidine" -> "H2 receptor antagonist" -> "possible side effects include cardiovascular effects" -> "can lead to tachycardia" -> 80%
analysis: Nizatidine is indeed a H2 receptor antagonist used primarily in the treatment of peptic ulcer disease and gastroesophageal reflux disease, aligning with option 'opa'. It does not have 100% bioavailability; rather, its bioavailability is approximately 70%, which contradicts option 'opb'. Nizatidine has been noted to have some effect on gastric motility, which could be interpreted as enhancing gastric emptying, supporting option 'opc'. There is no well-documented evidence linking nizatidine directly to causing tachycardia, making option 'opd' also incorrect. However, the most clearly incorrect statement based on pharmacological data is option 'opb'.
